rules: Searched every PubMed record in Europe PMC with potassium (potassium) in its title or abstract, in papers about supplements, salt substitutes, intake or diet; downloaded all reviews, randomised trials and guidelines.
Left out animal studies (MeSH tags, or the title when there are none) and retracted papers.
An outcome counts when its words are in the title.

Reviews: meta-analyses or systematic reviews of randomised trials of giving potassium, with potassium in the title, or in the abstract of a review of several supplements (not reviews of blood levels in observational studies; reviews without an abstract are kept for screening), and not about another group of people (such as sepsis, intensive care or surgery; each outcome's list is in the search definition). Chosen: the three newest meta-analyses (systematic reviews only if fewer than three), plus the most comprehensive one (most trials pooled, read from the abstract). Citations are shown but do not choose.
Newer large trials: randomised trials of at least 1,000 people (read from the abstract) from the year of the newest chosen review on, which those reviews may not include.

Screening: each eligible review's title and abstract was read against the finding's question (who, what was given, compared with what, what was measured) by Claude Code (opus), titles and abstracts only. Only reviews that answer it can be chosen; the others are listed with the reason. The decisions are kept in the repository and have not yet been checked by a clinician.
Overlap: the chosen reviews' reference lists (from Europe PMC) matched against the downloaded potassium trials, measured as the corrected covered area (Pieper 2014, PMID 24581293).

screening.by: Claude Code (opus), titles and abstracts only

left.title: Comparative effects of salt substitutes on blood pressure, cardiovascular events and mortality: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
left.reason: Potassium is given only as a salt substitute that also cuts sodium, compared with regular salt rather than placebo; the outcome includes blood pressure.

left.title: Effectiveness of self-monitoring devices measuring the urinary sodium-to-potassium ratio, urinary salt (sodium) excretion, or salt concentration in foods for blood pressure management: a systematic review and meta-analysis
left.reason: Tests self-monitoring devices for sodium and potassium, not potassium supplements at different doses.

left.title: Magnesium and Potassium Supplementation for Systolic Blood Pressure Reduction in the General Normotensive Population: A Systematic Review and Subgroup Meta-Analysis for Optimal Dosage and Treatment Length
left.reason: Placebo-controlled potassium trials with dose subgroups and blood pressure outcomes, but the population is normotensive rather than mostly hypertensive.

left.title: The impact of baseline potassium intake on the dose-response relation between sodium reduction and blood pressure change: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials
left.reason: Looks at sodium reduction and treats baseline potassium intake as a modifier, not potassium supplementation.

left.title: Effect of low-sodium salt substitutes on blood pressure, detected hypertension, stroke and mortality
left.reason: Potassium is given only within low-sodium salt substitutes, compared with regular salt; no dose-response for potassium supplements.

left.title: Oral potassium supplementation for management of essential hypertension: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
left.reason: Placebo-controlled potassium RCTs in essential hypertension with blood pressure outcomes, but no dose-response analysis is reported.

left.title: Nutraceuticals with a clinically detectable blood pressure-lowering effect: a review of available randomized clinical trials and their meta-analyses
left.reason: Narrative review of many nutraceuticals for blood pressure, with no pooled analysis of potassium dose.

left.title: Sodium-to-potassium ratio and blood pressure, hypertension, and related factors
left.reason: Narrative synthesis of the sodium-to-potassium ratio from RCTs and observational studies, with no pooling of potassium supplement doses.

left.title: Combined calcium, magnesium and potassium supplementation for the management of primary hypertension in adults
left.reason: Potassium is given only in combination with magnesium or calcium, in hypertensive adults; no dose-response analysis is reported.

left.title: Effects of oral potassium on blood pressure. Meta-analysis of randomized controlled clinical trials
left.reason: Pools RCTs of potassium supplements against control for blood pressure, but the population is mixed and no dose-response result is reported.
